I will keep my land in the usual Quzhou pattern: winter wheat followed by summer maize. I would not make this year complicated. I am 75, so I want crops I already know well, that fit the county’s climate, and that I can manage with steady labor. In Quzhou, the common system is still wheat-maize rotation, annual rainfall is only about 500 to 560 mm, and most of that rain comes in summer, so winter wheat needs several irrigations while summer maize can lean more on rainfall. Because of that, I will put my main effort into a stable wheat crop with controlled fertilizer and irrigation, then follow with hybrid summer maize using lighter irrigation and fewer sprays. I will keep the area modest at 8 mu so I can still manage it myself, use rotary tillage before wheat, switch to no-tillage for maize after wheat harvest to save time and moisture, and keep fertilizer around the moderate rates that match North China Plain field results rather than pushing excessive inputs. Sources used: Britannica on Hebei climate and agriculture, plus Quzhou / North China Plain field studies showing wheat-maize dominance, summer-rain concentration, and moderate N rates for wheat and maize: https://www.britannica.com/place/Hebei/Climate ; https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4395/13/11/2712 ; https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0959652614000304 ; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/37050116/ ; https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/32094371/
